kind: code (tier A: 2 lenses + skeptics on majors; phase-gate red-team-by-data >=20 deny spellings). Subagents read §3.5 (1334-1427) — the git deny matrix is normative; NEVER paraphrase it.

assertions.text: decideGit(command, sessionRole, gitMode, runActive, branchPolicy) -> {action: allow|deny, reason?}; DEFAULT-DENY for any subcommand not in the read-only allow-list or an explicit row
the FULL §3.5 matrix as a table, one test per row

verbatim guards: git add src/config.ts deny naming conductor_publish; git log --grep config allow; git stash push -m drop deny; git stash list allow; git commit -m "fix reset logic" deny-with-publish-reason (not destructive-verb false positive); echo hi && git reset --hard deny (every segment scanned); newline-separated compound deny; +refspec/:refspec push denies; restore --staged allow vs restore --staged --worktree deny

one test each: git apply patch.diff deny (most important row); worktree add deny; update-ref, symbolic-ref, sparse-checkout set, submodule update, bisect start, gc --prune=now, reflog expire, fetch, remote set-url, tag -d v1, config user.email x all deny
git blame, shortlog, describe, cat-file -p HEAD, rev-list --count HEAD, worktree list, config --get user.name all allow
invented subcommand git frobnicate denies by default with reason naming the subcommand
git switch feature: deny under branchPolicy pin with run active; allow under check-only; allow under pin with no active run
